subject_definitions:
@Image1 is the woman in the neon alley. Reference role: identity anchor. Keep exactly: chin-length blue hair with a magenta streak at the front, pale skin, a cropped grey denim jacket over a pale green tee, a black pleated mini skirt, a black cybernetic forearm brace, and the hip-shot lean against the graffiti wall. Do not carry over the wall text or the blurred crowd behind her.

summary:
[reference generation] One continuous five-second shot: the woman of @Image1 pushes off the alley wall, walks toward the lens through the neon crowd, and looks back into the camera without breaking her stride.

retention_analysis:
@Image1: fully_preserved - face, hair colour and front streak, jacket and its buttoned cuffs, tee, pleated skirt, forearm brace.
@Image1 pose and background: weak_reference only - the lean against the wall is just the start of the move, and the crowd behind her is replaced by new passers-by.

detailed_description:
Cyberpunk night-street cinematography, fast prime wide open, shallow depth of field with the signage collapsing into pink and cyan bokeh, wet asphalt holding vertical streaks of neon, fine grain, no lens flares.

[Shot 1] The woman of @Image1 rests her shoulder against the graffiti-covered wall in the left third of the frame, chin lifted, eyes on the street. The camera starts tight on the wall and tracks backward at walking pace as she pushes off and follows, her jacket swinging open, the pleated skirt catching the air, the forearm brace glinting as it passes under a pink sign. She moves through a knot of blurred pedestrians who part around her, and at about three and a half seconds she slows, half turns, and looks straight into the lens while still walking. The camera keeps retreating and holds on her face for the last beat as the sign above her changes from pink to cyan.

overall_soundscape:
Rain-wet street ambience, the hum of neon signage, footsteps and soft heels on wet pavement, a murmuring crowd, a distant car door and one bicycle bell rolling past behind the lens.

non_diegetic_music:
A slow dark synth pad over a single sub-bass pulse at walking tempo, no drums, ending on an unresolved chord as she looks into the camera.

## Pika H3 Flex: Reference to Video (API)

**Input Assets**
- [api_pika_h3_flex_r2v_input_1.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/api_pika_h3_flex_r2v_input_1.png)

## What this graph does

1. **Load Image** feeds the character sheet into `reference_images.image_1` on **Pika H3 Flex Reference to Video**.
2. **Pika H3 Flex Reference to Video** renders one clip with synchronized audio from the prompt plus the references.
3. **Save Video** writes `api_pika_h3_flex_r2v.mp4`.

## References

The node accepts up to 9 images, 3 videos and 3 audio clips (12 in total). Connect one and the next empty slot appears. At least one image or video is required. In the prompt the inputs are addressed by connection order:

- `@Image1` … `@Image9` (or `<Picture 1>` …)
- `@Video1` … `@Video3`
- `@Audio1` … `@Audio3` — audio attached to a connected video counts here too while `reference_video_audio` is on

## Prompt format

This template uses the H3 reference structure. Every section is plain text, one per block:

```text
subject_definitions: what each @ImageN is, and which features must survive.
summary: the whole clip in one or two sentences.
retention_analysis: per subject, fully_preserved / attribute_transfer / weak_reference.
detailed_description: the shot timeline, camera vocabulary and lighting.
overall_soundscape: diegetic sound only.
non_diegetic_music: audience-only score, N/A when there is none.
```

## Parameters

| Widget | What it does |
|---|---|
| `reference_video_audio` | Copies the sound of connected videos to the output. Turn it off for motion transfer onto new ambience or music. |
| `resolution` | `480p` to `4k`; `1080p` and above render at 768p and upscale once. |
| `aspect_ratio` | `auto` follows a reference video, otherwise the prompt. Reference images do not affect it, so this template pins `16:9`. |
| `duration` | 5 to 15 seconds; 5 s gives 124 frames, about 5.17 s. |
| `rewrite_prompt` | Lets the model expand the prompt first; the same seed then gives a different video each run. |
| `seed` | Same seed with rewrite off repeats the video exactly. |

## Gotchas

- Image-only references do not set the aspect ratio: keep `aspect_ratio` explicit when you want widescreen.
- Reference videos are billed per second up to 15 s in total, on top of the per-second output rate.
- Audio is generated with the picture, so the clip arrives cut-ready.
